title: Accelerating LLM Inference with Lossless Speculative Decoding Algorithms for Heterogeneous Vocabularies

problems.title: SLRS exact-reconstruction count is not the first-token proposal event
problems.source_claim_location: Lemma3.1 p6; AppendixC pp14-16; proof AppendixG pp21,23
assumptions: Complete draft vocabulary D2 over a,b; target character vocabulary
Stop after1 token, also first-token-determined stopping
problems.check: Enumerate all6 stopped paths and exact rational acceptance/output law
problems.result: 3 prefix-a paths versus claimed1; incomplete exact mass yields output1/2,1/2 instead of4/5,1/5
counterevidence: Theorem3.2 identity sound with actual normalized proposal
Exact segmentation count2^(m-1) sound for narrower event
Empirical SLEM/TLI unaffected by this diagnosis
problems.impact: Invalid SLRS proposal-computation/complexity derivation; no claim actual deployed samplers fail
problems.correction: Enumerate actual stopping-rule terminal paths including crossing tokens; general efficient implementation unresolved

independent_check.source_fidelity: Freshly viewed p.5 Algorithm 3 and Theorem 3.2, p.6 stopping-rule discussion/Section 3.4/Lemma 3.1, p.15 Appendix C exact Hello tree and its psi-computation caption, and p.21 proof of Lemma 3.1.
independent_check.operative_assumptions: Alphabet {a,b}; complete D2 has every nonempty string of length <=2; target vocabulary contains single characters. Both T-to-D* and D*-to-T* expressibility conditions hold. Use a valid S1 that stops after one draft token; the first target character is also already fixed under every continuation. Uniform q is strictly positive on D2; target p=(4/5,1/5).
independent_check.independent_reasoning: The stopped paths producing first target a are a,aa,ab, whereas exact reconstruction counts a only. Thus m=1 has three paths rather than 2^(m-1)=1 even under the favorable first-token-determined stopping interpretation. Fresh rational enumeration gives true psi=(1/2,1/2) and exact-string masses=(1/6,1/6). Substituting the latter accepts all proposals and yields (1/2,1/2); true psi gives accepted mass (1/2,1/5), rejection 3/10 on a and exact output p.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_alternatives: The lemma is correct for exact internal segmentations; the rejection identity is correct with actual normalized terminal-event mass. A no-stopping all-prefix interpretation is not a rescue because qualifying continuations are infinite and overlap. The paper itself discusses crossing-token remainders and postpones practical SLRS deployment.
independent_check.dependency_and_severity: Retain Major for the SLRS proposal-computation and complexity derivation connected to Theorem 3.2. This is not a blanket losslessness counterexample to correctly computed psi and does not implicate benchmarked SLEM/TLI implementations.
independent_check.repair_scope: Relabeling the combinatorial event fixes the count only. Correct SLRS probability requires actual mutually exclusive terminal paths, stopping decisions and autoregressive probabilities, including boundary crossings. General efficient computation remains unresolved.

problems.title: Ambiguous nontriviality condition in the strict EM comparison
problems.result: Unequal probabilities alone allow equality, but the Dirac example may violate non-triviality. The strict theorem is valid under the natural non-Dirac reading.
counterevidence: Non-trivial can mean non-Dirac; the proof invokes 0<p(t)<1, supporting that intended scope
problems.correction: Explicitly require at least two positive masses; exact sum-of-squares proof verified.

independent_check.source_fidelity: Freshly viewed Theorem 3.1 on pp.5 and21: the wording contains both non-trivial and existence of unequal probabilities. A focused search found no separate formal definition of non-trivial in the frozen source.
independent_check.operative_assumptions: p=q are normalized target/draft laws on the same vocabulary. The Dirac example satisfies unequal probabilities but may fail the independent non-trivial assumption; it cannot be presented as an unconditional theorem counterexample.
independent_check.independent_reasoning: Exact-match acceptance is sum p_t^2 and rejection-sampling acceptance is 1. Their difference is sum p_t(1-p_t), strictly positive exactly when at least two masses are positive. Thus the standard non-Dirac reading makes the theorem valid. p=(1,0) refutes only the unequal-probabilities condition considered on its own.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_alternatives: Non-trivial naturally can exclude a point mass; the source proof explicitly invokes 0<p(t)<1. This justified reading prevents retaining a demonstrated Minor theorem defect.
independent_check.dependency_and_severity: Narrow initial Minor to Needs Evidence / scope clarification. No substantive false theorem is established under the non-Dirac reading; paper-wide Major remains supported independently by P1.
independent_check.repair_scope: State explicitly that at least two tokens have positive probability. This gives the exact condition and also includes nondegenerate uniform distributions, without changing the proof.
